what: Cheniere Energy Partners owns the Sabine Pass liquefied natural gas terminal in Louisiana, one of the largest LNG export facilities in the world. It is controlled by Cheniere Energy and structured as a partnership.
customers: European and Asian utilities and energy companies under twenty-year contracts, plus spot cargo buyers.
money: contracted and spot cargoes from Sabine Pass
moat: Export capacity that costs tens of billions and years of permitting to build, with almost all of it sold under long-term fixed-fee contracts.
risks: Cheniere Energy controls it, so minority unitholders have limited influence
Spot gas prices affect the uncontracted portion
It is a partnership, which complicates tax reporting for some investors
opportunities: Revenue grew about 24% last year with a 34% operating margin
A distribution yield above 5% backed by fixed-fee contracts
Expansion at Sabine Pass would add contracted capacity
watch: Cargoes delivered and the fixed-fee share of revenue.
